exercise.name: Lying Alternate Frog Kick

reference.title: Lying Alternate Frog Kick
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; page could not be read at authoring time, movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip and knee flexion with the hips turned out, then extension; trunk held)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the knees come in, exhale as the legs kick out long.

prescription.progression: Lower the extended legs closer to the floor, then add a head and shoulder lift

cues.text: Lie flat, arms by your sides palms down, legs long.
Brace and lift the legs a little off the mat; low back stays down.
Draw one knee in toward the chest, knee turned out, heel toward the other leg.
Push the heel out until the leg is long beside the other one; switch legs.
Lower the legs to the mat and rest.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the legs extend
mistakes.fix: Kick out higher (legs at a steeper angle) or bend the knees a little more.

mistakes.mistake: Legs dropping to the mat between reps
mistakes.fix: Keep the heels hovering through the set.

mistakes.mistake: Knees collapsing together in the tuck
mistakes.fix: Turn the knees out, heels in.
Rest the head on the mat.

kinematics.norm: Legs hover a little off the floor at full extension (clinical opinion)
From near straight to beyond 90 degrees in the tuck (clinical opinion)
From straight to deeply bent in the tuck (clinical opinion)
Knees apart, heels close together (clinical opinion)
Pelvis stays on the mat (clinical opinion; McGill 1998)
About 1 s in and 0.8 s out (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #15158, Lying Alternate Frog Kick, video (movement reference)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Straight-leg and legs-off-the-floor work loads the low back through the hip flexors (McGill 1998). If the low back arches off the mat, bend the knees or shorten the range.
Low-back pain or disc problems: prefer dead bugs or bent-knee alternatives.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before dynamic trunk-flexion or legs-off-the-floor work.
modify: Keep the resting leg bent with the foot on the mat.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus hold the pelvis down while the legs are off the floor; bilateral leg work needs more abdominal effort than unilateral (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas holds the leg up and pulls the knee in (clinical opinion; Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas holds the leg up and pulls the knee in (clinical opinion; Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Straighten the knee on the kick.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Straighten the knee on the kick.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Bring the legs back together as they extend.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Bring the legs back together as they extend.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Brace the trunk against the moving legs.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Brace the trunk against the moving legs.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Turn the thigh out in the tuck (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Turn the thigh out in the tuck (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Heel draws in and kicks out
